passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: This section is an analysis of the financial performance and of significant trends that may affect TotalEnergies’ future performance and it should be read in conjunction with the Consolidated Financial Statements and the Notes thereto starting on page F-9. The Consolidated Financial Statements and the Notes thereto are prepared in accordance with IFRS as issued by the IASB and IFRS as adopted by the EU. The critical accounting estimates are disclosed in the paragraph "Major judgments and accounting estimates" of the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements. This section contains forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. For a list of important factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed in the forward-looking statements, see “Cautionary Statement Concerning Forward-Looking Statements” starting on page i. For information on the invasion of Ukraine by Russia and the situation of the Company at March 27, 2026, refer to “Item 5. – 5.6 Situation of the Company in Russia at March 27, 2026” below. 5.1 Overview TotalEnergies’ results are affected by a variety of factors, including changes in crude oil and natural gas prices and refining and marketing margins, all generally expressed in dollars, as well as changes in exchange rates, particularly the value of the euro compared to the dollar. Higher crude oil and natural gas prices generally have a positive effect on the income of TotalEnergies because the Exploration & Production segment’s oil and gas business and the Integrated LNG and downstream gas business are positively impacted by the resulting increase in revenues. Lower crude oil and natural gas prices generally have a corresponding negative effect. The effect of changes in crude oil prices on the activities of TotalEnergies’ Refining & Chemicals and Marketing & Services segments (Downstream) depends upon the speed at which the prices of refined petroleum products adjust to reflect such changes. TotalEnergies’ results are also significantly affected by the costs of its activities, in particular those related to exploration and production, and by the outcome of its strategic decisions with respect to cost reduction efforts. In addition, TotalEnergies’ results are affected by general economic and political conditions and changes in governmental laws and regulations, as well as by the impact of decisions by OPEC+ on production levels. For more information, refer to “Item 3. – 3.1 Risk factors”. In 2025, TotalEnergies reported IFRS net income of $13.1 billion, adjusted net income 1 of $15.6 billion, cash flow from operating activities of $27.3 billion and cash flow from operations excluding working capital (CFFO) 1 of $27.8 billion in an environment marked by a decline of 15% in oil prices. Return on average capital employed (ROACE) 1 stood at 12.6%, the best among the majors for the fourth consecutive year. TotalEnergies continued to implement its balanced, disciplined growth strategy by investing $17.1 billion in 2025, including 37% for new Oil & Gas projects and around $3.5 billion in low ‑ carbon energies, of which nearly $3 billion in electricity. credit_strengths.text: TotalEnergies generates substantial operating cash flow that comfortably covers its capital investment programme, even as oil prices declined. The company invested heavily in new Oil & Gas projects and low-carbon energies while still funding shareholder distributions, demonstrating resilient cash generation through the cycle. This supports the view that core operations remain the primary source of liquidity.

The company maintains a large cash balance and a broad, integrated energy footprint spanning Exploration & Production, Integrated LNG, Refining & Chemicals and Marketing & Services. This diversification across the value chain, combined with a strong ROACE relative to peers, underpins business resilience and provides a buffer against segment-specific volatility.

key_risks.text: Results are highly sensitive to crude oil and natural gas prices, refining margins and exchange rates. A decline in oil prices already pressured revenue and cash flow, and OPEC+ production decisions or further price weakness could materially reduce earnings and cash generation. This commodity price exposure is the dominant driver of credit quality.

The balance sheet shows no tagged borrowings, but lease liabilities are excluded from debt and short-term borrowings may be nil. A material data gap exists: interest expense, operating income and total debt are unavailable, preventing calculation of leverage and coverage. Without this information, the debt servicing capacity cannot be fully assessed.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Operating cash flow is strong relative to the company's cash position and investment needs, suggesting ample capacity to service obligations. However, the absence of reported debt and interest expense prevents a precise coverage calculation. The company's ability to generate cash through the cycle is the key support for debt service.

The current ratio sits slightly below one, indicating that current liabilities marginally exceed current assets. While this is not unusual for a large integrated energy company with substantial working capital swings, it warrants monitoring. The company's access to capital markets and undrawn facilities likely mitigates near-term liquidity pressure.

overall_credit_view.text: TotalEnergies' credit profile is supported by its scale, integrated business model and robust cash generation. The company invests heavily in both traditional and low-carbon energy while returning cash to shareholders. These factors suggest a solid investment-grade profile, though the absence of debt and interest data limits a full quantitative assessment.

Key risks include commodity price volatility and the material data gap on debt and interest expense. The company's leverage and coverage cannot be calculated from available tags, so the indicative risk profile remains incomplete. We would seek the debt note and interest expense disclosure to finalise the credit view.

credit_strengths.text: TotalEnergies產生可觀的營運現金流，即使油價下跌，仍能輕鬆覆蓋其資本投資計劃。該公司大力投資於新的油氣項目及低碳能源，同時仍能為股東分派提供資金，展現出貫穿週期的韌性現金產生能力。這支持了核心業務仍是流動性主要來源的觀點。
該公司維持龐大的現金結餘及廣泛的綜合能源業務版圖，涵蓋勘探與生產、綜合LNG、煉油與化工以及營銷與服務。這種跨越價值鏈的多元化，加上相對於同業強勁的ROACE，支撐了業務韌性，並為應對特定分部的波動提供了緩衝。

key_risks.text: 業績對原油及天然氣價格、煉油利潤率及匯率高度敏感。油價下跌已對收入及現金流構成壓力，而OPEC+的產量決定或價格進一步疲軟，可能大幅減少盈利及現金產生。這種商品價格風險是信用質量的主導驅動因素。
資產負債表顯示沒有標記的借款，但租賃負債從債務中排除，且短期借款可能為零。存在重大數據缺口：利息費用、營業利潤及總債務均無法獲得，導致無法計算槓桿及覆蓋率。缺乏此信息，債務償付能力無法全面評估。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 營運現金流相對於公司的現金狀況及投資需求而言強勁，表明有充裕能力償付債務。然而，缺乏報告的債務及利息費用，無法精確計算覆蓋率。公司貫穿週期產生現金的能力是債務償付的關鍵支撐。
流動比率略低於一，表明流動負債略高於流動資產。雖然這對一家營運資金波動較大的大型綜合能源公司而言並非異常，但仍值得監察。公司進入資本市場的渠道及未提取的融資額度，可能緩解短期流動性壓力。

overall_credit_view.text: TotalEnergies的信用狀況受到其規模、綜合業務模式及強勁現金產生能力的支撐。該公司大力投資於傳統及低碳能源，同時向股東返還現金。這些因素表明其擁有穩健的投資級狀況，儘管缺乏債務及利息數據限制了全面的定量評估。
主要風險包括商品價格波動以及債務和利息費用的重大數據缺口。公司的槓桿及覆蓋率無法從現有標籤計算，因此指示性風險狀況仍不完整。我們將尋求債務附註及利息費用披露，以最終確定信用觀點。
